About Us

Mandate, functions and history of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.

Ministry

  • About Us
  • Our Team
  • Our Divisions
  • Our Organisations
  • Our Performance
  • Directory

The Ministry of Tribal Affairs was constituted in October 1999, after the bifurcation of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, to provide a more focused approach to the integrated socio-economic development of Scheduled Tribes — among the most under-served sections of Indian society — in a coordinated and planned manner.

The Ministry is the nodal Ministry for overall policy, planning and coordination of programmes for the development of Scheduled Tribes. Its schemes are implemented through State Governments, Union Territory administrations, the Ministry’s organisations and voluntary organisations, and it works with other Ministries through convergence missions such as PM-JANMAN and Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan.

Functions of the Ministry

  • Overall policy, planning and coordination of programmes for the development of Scheduled Tribes, as the nodal Ministry.
  • Education of ST students: pre-matric, post-matric, top class, fellowship and overseas scholarships, and Eklavya Model Residential Schools.
  • Grants to States for tribal development: Special Central Assistance (PMAAGY), grants under Article 275(1), development of PVTGs, PM-JANMAN and Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan.
  • Livelihood, marketing of minor forest produce and tribal products, and concessional credit through TRIFED and NSTFDC.
  • Research, evaluation, statistics and training through Tribal Research Institutes and Centres of Excellence.
  • Promotion of voluntary efforts for tribal welfare through grants to voluntary organisations.
  • Scheduling and de-scheduling of tribes, Scheduled Areas, and the Panchayats (Extension to the Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996.
  • Nodal Ministry for the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006.
  • Monitoring of the Development Action Plan for Scheduled Tribes (Scheduled Tribe Component) of 41 Ministries and Departments.
  • Matters relating to the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes.

Constitutional framework

Constitutional provisions for Scheduled Tribes
ProvisionWhat it provides
Article 342The President specifies tribes or tribal communities as Scheduled Tribes for each State/UT by public notification; Parliament may include or exclude communities by law.
Article 46The State shall promote with special care the educational and economic interests of the weaker sections, in particular Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Article 244 and the Fifth & Sixth SchedulesAdministration of Scheduled Areas (Fifth Schedule) and of tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram (Sixth Schedule).
Article 275(1)Grants-in-aid from the Consolidated Fund of India to States for the welfare of Scheduled Tribes and for raising the level of administration of Scheduled Areas.
Articles 330 and 332Reservation of seats for Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies.
Article 338AThe National Commission for Scheduled Tribes.
